questions.question: The optimum cruise altitude is
choices: the pressure altitude up to which a cabin altitude of 8000 ft can be maintained.
the pressure altitude at which the speed for high speed buffet as TAS is a maximum.
the pressure altitude at which the best specific range can be achieved.
the pressure altitude at which the fuel flow is a maximum.
questions.answerText: the pressure altitude at which the best specific range can be achieved.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which statement with respect to the step climb is correct?
choices: A step climb is executed because ATC desires a higher altitude.
A step climb is executed in principle when, just after leveling off, the 1.3g altitude is reached.
Executing a desired step climb at high altitude can be limited by buffet onset at g-loads larger than 1.
A step climb must be executed immediately after the aeroplane has exceeded the optimum altitude.
questions.answerText: Executing a desired step climb at high altitude can be limited by buffet onset at g-loads larger than 1.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which speed provides maximum obstacle clearance during climb?
choices: The speed for which the ratio between rate of climb and forward speed is maximum.
The speed for maximum rate of climb.
questions.answerText: The speed for which the ratio between rate of climb and forward speed is maximum.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: On a reciprocating engined aeroplane, to maintain a given angle of attack, configuration and altitude at higher gross mass
choices: the airspeed and the drag will be increased.
the airspeed will be decreased and the drag increased.
the lift/drag ratio must be increased.
the airspeed will be increased but the drag does not change.
questions.answerText: the airspeed and the drag will be increased.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Given that: VEF= Critical engine failure speed VMCG= Ground minimum control speed VMCA= Air minimum control speed VMU= Minimum unstick speed V1= Take-off decision speed VR= Rotation speed V2 min.= Minimum take-off safety speed The correct formula is:
choices: 1.05 VMCA<= VEF<= V1
1.05 VMCG< VEF<= VR
V2min<= VEF<= VMU
VMCG<=VEF < V1
questions.answerText: VMCG<=VEF < V1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: At a given altitude, when a turbojet aeroplane mass is increased by 5% - assuming the engines specific consumption remains unchanged -, its hourly consumption is approximately increased by:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: The performance limited take-off mass is independant of the wind component.
The accelerate stop distance required is independant of the runway condition.
The take-off distance with one engine out is independant of the wind component.
The climb limited take-off mass is independant of the wind component.
questions.answerText: The climb limited take-off mass is independant of the wind component.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: A lower airspeed at constant mass and altitude requires
choices: less thrust and a lower coefficient of lift.
more thrust and a lower coefficient of lift.
more thrust and a lower coefficient of drag.
a higher coefficient of lift.
questions.answerText: a higher coefficient of lift.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: At a constant Mach number the thrust and the fuel flow of a jet engine
choices: increase in proportion to the ambient pressure at constant temperature.
decrease in proportion to the ambient pressure at constant temperature.
increase with increasing altitude.
are independent of outside air temperature (OAT).
questions.answerText: decrease in proportion to the ambient pressure at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Following a take-off determined by the 50ft (15m) screen height, a light twin climbs on a 10% over-the-ground climb gradient. It will clear a 900 m high obstacle in relation to the runway (horizontally), situated at 10 000 m from the 50 ft clearing point with an obstacle clearance of:
choices: It will not clear the obstacle
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Moving the center of gravity from the forward to the aft limit (gross mass, altitude and airspeed remain unchanged)
choices: increases the power required.
affects neither drag nor power required.
increases the induced drag.
decreases the induced drag and reduces the power required.
questions.answerText: decreases the induced drag and reduces the power required.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: On a reciprocating engined aeroplane, with increasing altitude at constant gross mass, angle of attack and configuraton the power required
choices: remains unchanged but the TAS increases.
increases and the TAS increases by the same percentage.
increases but TAS remains constant.
decreases slightly because of the lower air density.
questions.answerText: increases and the TAS increases by the same percentage.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: During certification test flights for a turbojet aeroplane, the actual measured take-off runs from brake release to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 feet above the take-off surface are: - 1747 m, all engines operating - 1950 m, with the critical engine failure recognized at V1, the other factors remaining unchanged. Considering both possibilities to determine the take-off run (TOR). What is the correct distance?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6586A or Flight planning Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.3 Table 2.3.1) Using the Power Setting Table, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the cruise TAS and fuel flow (lbs/hr) with full throttle and cruise lean mixture in the following conditions: Given : OAT: 3°C Pressure altitude: 6000 ft Power: Full throttle / 21,0 in/Hg./ 2100 RPM
choices: 131 kt and 56,9 lbs/hr
125 kt and 55,7 lbs/hr
134 kt and 55,7 lbs/hr
136 kt and 56,9 lbs/hr
questions.answerText: 134 kt and 55,7 lbs/hr
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-3589A or Performance Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.24) With regard to the drift down performance of the twin jet aeroplane, why does the curve representing 35 000 kg gross mass in the chart for drift down net profiles start at approximately 3 minutes at FL370?
choices: Because at this mass the engines slow down at a slower rate after failure, there is still some thrust left during four minutes.
Due to higher TAS at this mass it takes more time to develop the optimal rate of descent, because of the inertia involved.
All the curves start at the same point, which is situated outside the chart.
Because at this mass it takes about 3 minutes to decelerate to the optimum speed for drift down at the original cruising level.
questions.answerText: Because at this mass it takes about 3 minutes to decelerate to the optimum speed for drift down at the original cruising level.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Assuming that the required lift exists, which forces determine an aeroplane's angle of climb?
choices: Thrust and drag only.
Weight and thrust only.
Weight, drag and thrust.
Weight and drag only.
questions.answerText: Weight, drag and thrust.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The point at which a tangent out of the origin touches the power required curve
choices: is the point where Drag coefficient is a minimum.
is the point where the Lift to Drag ratio is a minimum.
is the maximum drag speed.
is the point where the Lift to Drag ratio is a maximum.
questions.answerText: is the point where the Lift to Drag ratio is a maximum.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: How does the best angle of climb and best rate of climb vary with increasing altitude?
choices: Both decrease.
Both increase.
Best angle of climb increases while best rate of climb decreases.
Best angle of climb decreases while best rate of climb increases.
questions.answerText: Both decrease.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which statement related to a take-off from a wet runway is correct?
choices: In case of a reverser inoperative the wet runway performance information can still be used
Screenheight reduction can not be applied because of reduction in obstacle clearance.
A reduction of screen height is allowed in order to reduce weight penalties
The use of a reduced Vr is sufficient to maitain the same safety margins as for a dry runway
questions.answerText: A reduction of screen height is allowed in order to reduce weight penalties
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Reduced take-off thrust should normally not be used when:
choices: it is dark.
the runway is dry.
the runway is wet.
windshear is reported on the take-off path.
questions.answerText: windshear is reported on the take-off path.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The long range cruise speed is in relation to the speed for maximum range cruise.
choices: Lower
Depending on the OAT and net mass.
Depending on density altitude and mass.
Higher
questions.answerText: Higher
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6585A or Flight planning Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.2 Table 2.2.3) Using the Power Setting Table, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the cruise TAS and fuel flow (lbs/hr) with full throttle and cruise lean mixture in the following conditions: Given: OAT: 13°C Pressure altitude: 8000 ft RPM: 2300
choices: 160 kt and 71,1 lbs/hr
159 kt and 71,7 lbs/hr
160 kt and 69,3 lbs/hr
158 kt and 74,4 lbs/hr
questions.answerText: 160 kt and 69,3 lbs/hr
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The rate of climb
choices: is approximately climb gradient times true airspeed divided by 100.
is the downhill component of the true airspeed.
is angle of climb times true airspeed.
is the horizontal component of the true airspeed.
questions.answerText: is approximately climb gradient times true airspeed divided by 100.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The maximum horizontal speed occurs when:
choices: The thrust is equal to minimum drag.
The thrust does not increase further with increasing speed.
The maximum thrust is equal to the total drag.
The thrust is equal to the maximum drag.
questions.answerText: The maximum thrust is equal to the total drag.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6575A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.1) With regard to the take off performance chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the maximum allowable take off mass . Given : O.A.T : ISA Pressure Altitude: 4000 ft Headwind component: 5 kt Flaps: up Runway: Tarred and Dry Factored runway length: 2000 ft Obstacle height: 50 ft
choices: 3000 lbs
2900 lbs
3240 lbs
questions.answerText: 3240 lbs
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The required Take-off Distance (TOD) and the field length limited Take-off Mass (TOM) are different for the zero flap case and take-off position flap case. What is the result of flap setting in take-off position compared to zero flap position?
choices: Increased TOD required and decreased field length limited TOM.
Increased TOD required and increased field length limited TOM.
Decreased TOD required and decreased field length limited TOM.
Decreased TOD required and increased field length limited TOM.
questions.answerText: Decreased TOD required and increased field length limited TOM.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
choices: VR must not be less than 1.05 VMCA and not less than 1.1 V1.
VR must not be less than 1.05 VMCA and not less than V1.
VR must not be less than VMCA and not less than 1.05 V1.
VR must not be less than 1.1 VMCA and not less than V1.
questions.answerText: VR must not be less than 1.05 VMCA and not less than V1.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The optimum altitude
choices: is the altitude up to which cabin pressure of 8 000 ft can be maintained.
increases as mass decreases and is the altitude at which the specific range reaches its maximum.
decreases as mass decreases.
is the altitude at which the specific range reaches its minimum.
questions.answerText: increases as mass decreases and is the altitude at which the specific range reaches its maximum.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Considering TAS for maximum range and maximum endurance, other factors remaining constant,
choices: TAS for maximum range will increase with increased altitude while TAS for maximum endurance will decrease with increased altitude.
both will increase with increasing altitude.
both will decrease with increasing altitude.
both will stay constant regardless of altitude.
questions.answerText: both will increase with increasing altitude.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The climb gradient of an aircraft after take-off is 6% in standard atmosphere, no wind, at 0 ft pressure altitude. Using the following corrections: "± 0,2 % / 1 000 ft field elevation" "± 0,1 % / °C from standard temperature" " - 1 % with wing anti-ice" " - 0,5% with engine anti-ice" The climb gradient after take-off from an airport situated at 1 000 ft, 17° C; QNH 1013,25 hPa, with wing and engine anti-ice operating for a functional check is :
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements concerning drift- down is correct?
choices: The drift-down procedure requires a minimum descent angle after an engine failure at cruising altitude.
The drift-down procedure requires a minimum obstacle clearance of 35 ft.
An engine failure at high cruising altitude will always result in a drift-down, because it is not permitted to fly the same altitude with one engine inoperative as with all engines operating.
When determining the obstacle clearance during drift-down, fuel dumping may be taken into account.
questions.answerText: When determining the obstacle clearance during drift-down, fuel dumping may be taken into account.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Two identical turbojet aeroplanes (whose specific fuel consumption is assumed to be constant) are in a holding pattern at the same altitude. The mass of the first one is 95 000 kg and its hourly fuel consumption is equal to 3100 kg/h. Since the mass of the second one is 105 000 kg, its hourly fuel consumption is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: As long as an aeroplane is in a positive climb
choices: VX is always below VY.
VX is sometimes below and sometimes above VY depending on altitude.
VX is always above VY.
VY is always above VMO.
questions.answerText: VX is always below VY.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: What is the advantage of balancing V1, even in the event of a climb limited take-off?
choices: The safety margin with respect to the runway length is greatest.
The take-off distance required with one engine out at V1 is the shortest.
The accelerate stop distance required is the shortest.
The climb limited take-off mass is the highest.
questions.answerText: The safety margin with respect to the runway length is greatest.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: What happens to the drag of a jet aeroplane if, during the initial climb after take off, constant IAS is maintained? (Assume a constant mass.)
choices: The drag decreases.
The drag increases initially and decreases thereafter.
The drag remains almost constant.
The drag increases considerably.
questions.answerText: The drag remains almost constant.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The point where Drag coefficient/Lift coefficient is a minimum is
choices: at stalling speed (VS).
on the "back side" of the drag curve.
the point where a tangent from the origin touches the drag curve.
the lowest point of the drag curve.
questions.answerText: the point where a tangent from the origin touches the drag curve.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The speed VR
choices: must be higher than VLOF.
must be equal to or lower than V1.
is the speed at which rotation to the lift-off angle of attack is initiated.
must be higher than V2.
questions.answerText: is the speed at which rotation to the lift-off angle of attack is initiated.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: At a given mass, the stalli ng speed of a twin engine aircraft is 100 kt in the landing configuration. The minimum speed a pilot must maintain in short final is:
choices: 130 kt
115 kt
125 kt
120 kt
questions.answerText: 130 kt
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: In case of an engine failure which is recognized at or above V1
choices: the take-off should be rejected if the speed is still below VR.
the take-off must be continued.
the take-off must be rejected if the speed is still below VLOF.
a height of 50 ft must be reached within the take-off distance.
questions.answerText: the take-off must be continued.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: For take-off obstacle clearance calculations, obstacles in the first segment may be avoided
choices: by banking not more than 15° between 50 ft and 400 ft above the runway elevation.
by banking as much as needed if aeroplane is more than 50 ft above runway elevation.
only by using standard turns.
by standard turns - but only after passing 1500 ft.
questions.answerText: by banking not more than 15° between 50 ft and 400 ft above the runway elevation.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The Density Altitude
choices: is used to calculate the FL above the Transition Altitude.
is used to determine the aeroplane performance.
is equal to the pressure altitude.
is used to establish minimum clearance of 2.000 feet over mountains.
questions.answerText: is used to determine the aeroplane performance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following factors leads to the maximum flight time of a glide?
choices: Low mass.
High mass.
Headwind.
Tailwind.
questions.answerText: Low mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A constant headwind
choices: increases the descent distance over ground.
increases the angle of the descent flight path.
increases the angle of descent.
increases the rate of descent.
questions.answerText: increases the angle of the descent flight path.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The second segment begins
choices: when landing gear is fully retracted.
when flap retraction begins.
when flaps are selected up.
when acceleration starts from V2 to the speed for flap retraction.
questions.answerText: when landing gear is fully retracted.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The stalling speed or the minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane is controllable in landing configuration is abbreviated as
choices: VS1.
VS.
VMC.
VSO.
questions.answerText: VSO.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: If the take-off mass of an aeroplane is tyre speed limited, downhill slope would
choices: increase the maximum mass for take-off.
increase the required take-off distance.
have no effect on the maximum mass for take-off.
decrease the maximum mass for take-off.
questions.answerText: have no effect on the maximum mass for take-off.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: What will be the effect on an aeroplane's performance if aerodrome pressure altitude is decreased?
choices: It will increase the take-off distance required.
It will increase the take-off ground run.
It will increase the accelerate stop distance.
It will decrease the take-off distance required.
questions.answerText: It will decrease the take-off distance required.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane carries out a descent from FL 410 to FL 270 at cruise Mach number, and from FL 270 to FL 100 at the IAS reached at FL 270. How does the angle of descent change in the first and in the second part of the descent? Assume idle thrust and clean configuration and ignore compressibilit y effects.
choices: Increases in the first part; is constant in the second.
Increases in the first part; decreases in the second.
Is constant in the first part; decreases in the second.
Decreases in the first part; increases in the second.
questions.answerText: Increases in the first part; is constant in the second.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A constant headwind component
choices: increases the angle of flight path during climb.
increases the best rate of climb.
decreases the angle of climb.
increases the maximum endurance.
questions.answerText: increases the angle of flight path during climb.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Higher gross mass at the same altitude decreases the gradient and the rate of climb whereas
choices: VY and VX are increased.
VX is increased and VY is decreased.
VY and VX are not affected by a higher gross mass.
VY and VX are decreased.
questions.answerText: VY and VX are increased.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: For a turboprop powered aeroplane, a 2200 m long runway at the destination aerodrome is expected to be "wet". The "dry runway" landing distance, should not exceed:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Maximum endurance for a piston engined aeroplane is achieved at:
choices: The speed that approximately corresponds to the maximum rate of climb speed.
The speed for maximum lift coefficient.
The speed for minimum drag.
The speed that corresponds to the speed for maximum climb angle.
questions.answerText: The speed that approximately corresponds to the maximum rate of climb speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: When the outside air temperature increases, then
choices: the field length limited take-off mass decreases but the climb limited take-off mass increases.
the field length limited take-off mass increases but the climb limited take-off mass decreases.
the field length limited take-off mass and the climb limited take-off mass decreases.
the field length limited take-off mass and the climb limited take-off mass increases.
questions.answerText: the field length limited take-off mass and the climb limited take-off mass decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: If the level-off altitude is below the obstacle clearance altitude during a drift down procedure
choices: fuel jettisoning should be started at the beginning of drift down.
the recommended drift down speed should be disregarded and it should be flown at the stall speed plus 10 kt.
fuel jettisoning should be started when the obstacle clearance altitude is reached.
the drift down should be flown with flaps in the approach configuration.
questions.answerText: fuel jettisoning should be started at the beginning of drift down.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: After engine failure the aeroplane is unable to maintain its cruising altitude. What is the procedure which should be applied?
choices: Emergency Descent Procedure.
ETOPS.
Long Range Cruise Descent.
Drift Down Procedure.
questions.answerText: Drift Down Procedure.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: With all engines out, a pilot wants to fly for maximum time. Therefore he has to fly the speed corresponding to:
choices: the minimum drag.
the critical Mach number.
the minimum angle of descent.
the maximum lift.
questions.answerText: the minimum drag.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements with regard to the actual acceleration height at the beginning of the 3rd climb segment is correct?
choices: The minimum value according to regulations is 1000 ft.
There is no legal minimum value, because this will be determined from case to case during the calculation of the net flight path.
The minimum value according to regulations is 400 ft.
A lower height than 400 ft is allowed in special circumstances e.g. noise abatement.
questions.answerText: The minimum value according to regulations is 400 ft.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The take-off distance available is
choices: the total runway length, without clearway even if this one exists.
the length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway available.
the runway length minus stopway.
the runway length plus half of the clearway.
questions.answerText: the length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: At constant thrust and constant altitude the fuel flow of a jet engine
choices: increases slightly with increasing airspeed.
is independent of the airspeed.
decreases slightly with increasing airspeed.
increases with decreasing OAT.
questions.answerText: increases slightly with increasing airspeed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: During certification flight testing on a four engine turbojet aeroplane the actual take-off distances measured are: - 3050 m with failure of the critical engine recognised at - 2555 m with all engines operating and all other things being equal The take-off distance adopted for the certification file is: V1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6570A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.4) With regard to the landing chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the landing distance from a height of 50 ft . Given : O.A.T : ISA +15°C Pressure Altitude: 0 ft Aeroplane Mass: 2940 lbs Tailwind component: 10 kt Flaps: Landing position (down) Runway: Tarred and Dry
choices: approximately : 950 feet
approximately : 1400 feet
approximately : 750 feet
approximately : 1300 feet
questions.answerText: approximately : 1300 feet
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: On a long distance flight the gross mass decreases continuously as a consequence of the fuel consumption. The result is:
choices: The speed must be increased to compensate the lower mass.
The specific range increases and the optimum altitude decreases.
The specific range decreases and the optimum altitude increases.
The specific range and the optimum altitude increases.
questions.answerText: The specific range and the optimum altitude increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6582A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.3) Using the climb performance chart, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the ground distance to reach a height of 1500 ft above the reference zero inthe following conditions: Given : O.A.T at Take-o Airport pressure altitude: 5000 ft Aeroplane mass: 3300 lbs Speed: 100 KIAS Wind component: 5 kts Tailwind ff: ISA
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The drift down requirements are based on:
choices: the actual engine thrust output at the altitude of engine failure.
the maximum flight path gradient during the descent.
the landing mass limit at the alternate.
the obstacle clearance during a descent to the new cruising altitude if an engine has failed.
questions.answerText: the obstacle clearance during a descent to the new cruising altitude if an engine has failed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane executes a steady glide at the speed for minimum glide angle. If the forward speed is kept constant, what is the effect of a lower mass? Rate of descent / Glide angle / CL/CD ratio
choices: decreases / constant / decreases
increases / increases / constant
increases / constant / increases
increases / increases / decreases
questions.answerText: increases / increases / decreases
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Induced drag decreases with increasing speed.
Induced drag increases with increasing speed.
Induced drag is independant of the speed.
Induced drag decreases with increasing angle of attack.
questions.answerText: Induced drag decreases with increasing speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A flight is planned with a turbojet aeroplane to an aerodrome with a landing distance available of 2400 m. Which of the following is the maximum landing distance for a dry runway?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: How does the thrust of fixed propeller vary during take- off run ? The thrust
choices: increases slightly while the aeroplane speed builds up.
varies with mass changes only.
has no change during take-off and climb.
decreases slightly while the aeroplane speed builds up.
questions.answerText: decreases slightly while the aeroplane speed builds up.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: VR is the speed at which, during rotation, the nose wheel comes off the runway.
VR is the speed at which the pilot should start to rotate the aeroplane.
VR should not be higher than V1.
VR should not be higher than 1.05 VMCG.
questions.answerText: VR is the speed at which the pilot should start to rotate the aeroplane.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Field length is balanced when
choices: one engine acceleration from V1 to VLOF plus flare distance between VLOF and 35 feet are equal.
take-off distance equals accelerate-stop distance.
calculated V2 is less than 110% VMCA and V1, VR, VMCG.
all engine acceleration to V1 and braking distance for rejected take-off are equal.
questions.answerText: take-off distance equals accelerate-stop distance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-1562A or Performance Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.4 ) For a twin engine turbojet aeroplane two take-off flap settings (5° and 15°) are certified. Given: Field length avalaible= 2400 m Outside air temperature= -10°C Airport pressure altitude= 7000 ft The maximum allowed take-off mass is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following answers is true?
choices: V1 > VR
V1 < VMCG
V1 <= VR
V1 > Vlof
questions.answerText: V1 <= VR
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6580A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.2) With regard to the take off performance chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the take off distance over a 50 ft obstacle height. Given : O.A.T : 30°C Pressure Altitude: 1000 ft Aeroplane Mass: 2950 lbs Tailwind component: 5 kt Flaps: Approach setting Runway: Short, wet grass, firm subsoil Correction factor: 1.25 (for runway conditions)
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane is climbing at constant Mach number below the tropopause. Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: IAS decreases and TAS decreases.
IAS increases and TAS increases.
IAS decreases and TAS increases.
IAS increases and TAS decreases.
questions.answerText: IAS decreases and TAS decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Regarding take-off, the take-off decision speed V1:
choices: is the airspeed of the aeroplane upon reaching 35 feet above the take-off surface.
is the airspeed on the ground at which the pilot is assumed to have made a decision to continue or discontinue the take- off.
is always equal to VEF (Engine Failure speed).
is an airspeed at which the aeroplane is airborne but below 35 ft and the pilot is assumed to have made a decision to continue or discontinue the take-off .
questions.answerText: is the airspeed on the ground at which the pilot is assumed to have made a decision to continue or discontinue the take- off.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Given a jet aircraft. Which order of increasing speeds in the performance diagram is correct?
choices: Vs, Maximum range speed, Vx
Maximum endurance speed, Maximum range speed, Vx
Vs, Vx, Maximum range speed
Maximum endurance speed, Long range speed, Maximum range speed
questions.answerText: Vs, Vx, Maximum range speed
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: If the climb speed schedule is changed from 280/.74 to 290/.74 the new crossover altitude is
choices: unchanged.
only affected by the aeroplane gross mass.
lower.
higher.
questions.answerText: lower.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Reduced take-off thrust should normally not be used when:
choices: it is dark.
the runway is wet.
obstacles are present close to the end of the runway.
the runway is contaminated.
questions.answerText: the runway is contaminated.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which data can be extracted from the Buffet Onset Boundary Chart?
choices: The value of the Mach number at which low speed and shockstall occur at various weights and altitudes.
The values of the Mach number at which low speed and Mach buffet occur at various masses and altitudes.
The value of maximum operating Mach number (MMO) at various masses and power settings.
The value of the critical Mach number at various masses and altitudes.
questions.answerText: The values of the Mach number at which low speed and Mach buffet occur at various masses and altitudes.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: With zero wind, the angle of attack for maximum range for an aeroplane with turbojet engines is:
choices: equal to that of maximum lift to drag ratio.
equal to that maximum endurance.
equal to that corresponding to zero induced drag.
lower than that of maximum lift to drag ratio.
questions.answerText: equal to that of maximum lift to drag ratio.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The speed V2 is defined for jet aeroplane as
choices: take-off climb speed or speed at 35 ft.
lift off speed.
take-off decision speed.
critical engine failure speed.
questions.answerText: take-off climb speed or speed at 35 ft.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: An increase in atmospheric pressure has, among other things, the following consequences on take-off performance:
choices: a reduced take-off distance and degraded initial climb performance
a reduced take-off distance and improved initial climb performance
an increases take-off distance and degraded initial climb performance
an increased take-off distance and improved initial climb performance
questions.answerText: a reduced take-off distance and improved initial climb performance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The induced drag of an aeroplane at constant gross weight and altitude is highest at
choices: VSO (stalling speed in landing configuration)
VS1 (stalling speed in clean configuration)
VMO (maximum operating limit speed)
VA (design manoeuvring speed)
questions.answerText: VSO (stalling speed in landing configuration)
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: On a twin engined piston aircraft with variable pitch propellers, for a given mass and altitude, the minimum drag speed is 125 kt and the holding speed (minimum fuel burn per hour) is 95 kt. The best rate of climb speed will be obtained for a speed:
choices: inferior to 95 kts
is between 95 and 125 kt
equal to 125 kt
equal to 95 kt
questions.answerText: equal to 95 kt
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: How does TAS vary in a constant Mach climb in the troposphere?
choices: TAS increases.
TAS is constant.
TAS is not related to Mach Number.
TAS decreases.
questions.answerText: TAS decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: In a steady descending flight (descent angle GAMMA) equilibrium of forces acting on the aeroplane is given by: (T = Thrust, D = Drag, W = Weight)
choices: T + D = - W sin GAMMA
T + W sin GAMMA = D
T - W sin GAMMA = D
T - D = W sin GAMMA
questions.answerText: T + W sin GAMMA = D
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The danger associated with low speed and/or high speed buffet
choices: limits the maneuvering load factor at high altitudes.
can be reduced by increasing the load factor.
exists only above MMO.
has to be considered at take-off and landing.
questions.answerText: limits the maneuvering load factor at high altitudes.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The pilot of a light twin engine aircraft has calculated a 4 000 m service ceiling, based on the forecast general conditions for the flight and a take-off mass of 3 250 kg. If the take-off mass is 3 000 kg, the service ceiling will be:
choices: less than 4 000 m.
unchanged, equal to 4 000 m.
only a new performance analysis will determine if the service ceiling is higher or lower than 4 000 m.
higher than 4 000 m.
questions.answerText: higher than 4 000 m.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Consider the graphic representation of the power required versus true air speed (TAS), for a jet aeroplane with a given mass. When drawing the tangent out of the origin, the point of contact determines the speed of:
choices: critical angle of attack.
maximum endurance.
minimum power.
maximum specific range.
questions.answerText: maximum endurance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ?
choices: If a clearway or a stopway is used, the liftoff point must be attainable at least at the end of the permanent runway surface.
A stopway means an area beyond the take-off runway, able to support the aeroplane during an aborted take-off.
An underrun is an area beyond the runway end which can be used for an aborted take-off.
A clearway is an area beyond the runway which can be used for an aborted take-off.
questions.answerText: A stopway means an area beyond the take-off runway, able to support the aeroplane during an aborted take-off.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: What effect has a downhill slope on the take-off speeds? The slope
choices: has no effect on the take-off speed V1.
decreases the take-off speed V1.
decreases the TAS for take-off.
increases the IAS for take-off.
questions.answerText: decreases the take-off speed V1.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The load factor in a turn in level flight with constant TAS depends on
choices: the radius of the turn and the bank angle.
the true airspeed and the bank angle.
the radius of the turn and the weight of the aeroplane.
the bank angle only.
questions.answerText: the bank angle only.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following factors determines the maximum flight altitude in the "Buffet Onset Boundary" graph?
choices: Aerodynamics.
Theoretical ceiling.
Service ceiling.
Economy.
questions.answerText: Aerodynamics.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-2211A) Which of the following diagrams correctly shows the movement of the power required curve with increasing altitude .(H1 < H2)
choices: Figure c
Figure a
Figure d
Figure b
questions.answerText: Figure d
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: What is the most important aspect of the 'backside of the power curve'?
choices: The elevator must be pulled to lower the nose.
The speed is unstable.
The aeroplane will not stall.
The altitude cannot be maintained.
questions.answerText: The speed is unstable.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The speed for best rate of climb is called
choices: VO.
VY.
VX.
questions.answerText: VY.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6588A or Flight planning Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.4) Using the Range Profile Diagramm, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the range, with 45 minutes reserve, in the following conditions: Given : O.A.T.: ISA -15°C Pressure altitude: 12000 ft Power: Full throttle / 23,0 in/Hg./ 2300 RPM
choices: 908 NM
902 NM
875 NM
860 NM
questions.answerText: 902 NM
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not affected by a tail wind?
choices: the field limited take-off mass.
the obstacle limited take-off mass.
the take-off run.
the climb limited take-off mass.
questions.answerText: the climb limited take-off mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: During the certification flight testing of a twin engine turbojet aeroplane, the real take-off distances are equal to: - 1547 m with all engines running - 1720 m with failure of critical engine at V1, with all other things remaining unchanged. The take-off distance adopted for the certification file is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The minimum value of V2 must exceed "air minimum control speed" by:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6577A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.1) With regard to the take off performance chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the take off speed for (1) rotation and (2) at a height of 50 ft. Given : O.A.T : ISA+10°C Pressure Altitude: 5000 ft Aeroplane mass: 3400 lbs Headwind component: 5 kt Flaps: up Runway: Tarred and Dry
choices: 73 and 84 KIAS
68 and 78 KIAS
65 and 75 KIAS
71 and 82 KIAS
questions.answerText: 71 and 82 KIAS
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: With regard to a take-off from a wet runway, which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Screen height cannot be reduced.
The screen height can be lowered to reduce the mass penalties.
When the runway is wet, the V1 reduction is sufficient to maintain the same margins on the runway length.
In case of a reverser inoperative the wet runway performance information can still be used.
questions.answerText: The screen height can be lowered to reduce the mass penalties.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: On a reciprocating engined aeroplane, to maintain a given angle of attack, configuration and altitude at higher gross mass
choices: an increase in airspeed is required but power setting does not change.
requires an increase in power and decrease in the airspeed.
an increase in airspeed and power is required.
a higher coefficient of drag is required.
questions.answerText: an increase in airspeed and power is required.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The first segment of the take-off flight path ends
choices: at completion of gear retraction.
at completion of flap retraction.
at reaching V2.
at 35 ft above the runway.
questions.answerText: at completion of gear retraction.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following factors favours the selection of a low flap setting for the take-off?
choices: High field elevation, no obstacles in the climb-out path, low ambient temperature and short runway.
Low field elevation, no obstacles in the climb-out path, short runway and a low ambient temperature.
High field elevation, distant obstacles in the climb-out path, long runway and a high ambient temperature.
Low field elevation, close-in obstacles in the climb-out path, long runway and a high ambient temperature.
questions.answerText: High field elevation, distant obstacles in the climb-out path, long runway and a high ambient temperature.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Balanced V1 is selected
choices: for a runway length limited take-off with a clearway to give the highest mass.
if it is equal to V2.
if the accelerate stop distance is equal to the one engine out take-off distance.
for a runway length limited take-off with a stopway to give the highest mass.
questions.answerText: if the accelerate stop distance is equal to the one engine out take-off distance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the influence of a runway down-slope is correct for a balanced take-off? Down- slope...
choices: increases V1 and reduces the accelerate stop distance required (ASDR).
reduces V1 and increases the accelerate stop distance required (ASDR).
increases V1 and increases the take-off distance required (TODR).
reduces V1 and reduces take-off distance required (TODR).
questions.answerText: reduces V1 and reduces take-off distance required (TODR).
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: For jet-engined aeroplanes, what is the effect of increased altitude on specific range?
choices: Does not change.
Increases only if there is no wind.
Increases.
Decreases.
questions.answerText: Increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Maximum and minimum values of V1 are limited by :
choices: VR and VMCG
V2 and VMCA
VR and VMCA
V2 and VMCG
questions.answerText: VR and VMCG
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Two identical aeroplanes at different masses are descending at idle thrust. Which of the following statements correctly describes their descent characteristics ?
choices: At a given angle of attack, both the vertical and the forward speed are greater for the heavier aeroplane.
There is no difference between the descent characteristics of the two aeroplanes.
At a given angle of attack the heavier aeroplane will always glide further than the lighter aeroplane.
At a given angle of attack the lighter aeroplane will always glide further than the heavier aeroplane.
questions.answerText: At a given angle of attack, both the vertical and the forward speed are greater for the heavier aeroplane.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: ETOPS flight is a twin engine jet aeroplane flight conducted over a route, where no suitable airport is within an area of
choices: 75 minutes flying time at the approved one engine out cruise speed.
60 minutes flying time in still air at the approved one engine out cruise speed.
60 minutes flying time in still air at the normal cruising speed.
30 minutes flying time at the normal cruising speed.
questions.answerText: 60 minutes flying time in still air at the approved one engine out cruise speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: For a take-off from a contaminated runway, which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Dry snow is not considered to affect the take-off performance.
A slush covered runway must be cleared before take-off, even if the performance data for contaminated runway is available.
The performance data for take-off must be determined in general by means of calculation, only a few values are verified by flight tests.
The greater the depth of contamination at constant take-off mass, the more V1 has to be decreased to compensate for decreasing friction.
questions.answerText: The performance data for take-off must be determined in general by means of calculation, only a few values are verified by flight tests.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: If the thrust available exceeds the thrust required for level flight
choices: the aeroplane accelerates if the altitude is maintained.
the aeroplane descends if the airspeed is maintained.
the aeroplane decelerates if it is in the region of reversed command.
the aeroplane decelerates if the altitude is maintained.
questions.answerText: the aeroplane accelerates if the altitude is maintained.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the relationship between traffic load and range is correct?
choices: The maximum landing mass is basically equal to the maximum zero fuel mass.
The maximum traffic load is not limited by the reserve fuel quantity.
The traffic load can be limited by the desired range.
The maximum zero fuel mass limits the maximum quantity of fuel.
questions.answerText: The traffic load can be limited by the desired range.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The induced drag of an aeroplane
choices: is independent of the airspeed.
increases with increasing airspeed.
decreases with increasing airspeed.
decreases with increasing gross weight.
questions.answerText: decreases with increasing airspeed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which statement, in relation to the climb limited take-off mass of a jet aeroplane, is correct?
choices: 50% of a head wind is taken into account when determining the climb limited take-off mass.
On high elevation airports equipped with long runways the aeroplane will always be climb limited.
The climb limited take-off mass decreases with increasing OAT.
The climb limited take-off mass is determined at the speed for best rate of climb.
questions.answerText: The climb limited take-off mass decreases with increasing OAT.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: How is V2 affected if T/O flaps 20° is chosen instead of T/O flaps 10°?
choices: V2 increases in proportion to the angle at which the flaps are set.
V2 has no connection with T/O flap setting, as it is a function of runway length only.
V2 decreases if not restricted by VMCA.
V2 has the same value in both cases.
questions.answerText: V2 decreases if not restricted by VMCA.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the jet engine ratings below is not a certified rating?
choices: Go-Around Thrust
Maximum Take-off Thrust
Maximum Cruise Thrust
Maximum Continuous Thrust
questions.answerText: Maximum Cruise Thrust
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: In the drag versus TAS curve for a jet aeroplane, the speed for maximum range corresponds with:
choices: the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the drag curve.
the point of intersection of the parasite drag curve and the induced drag curve.
the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the parasite drag curve.
the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the induced drag curve.
questions.answerText: the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the drag curve.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The drift down procedure specifies requirements concerning the:
choices: engine power at the altitude at which engine failure occurs
climb gradient during the descent to the net level-off altitude
weight during landing at the alternate
obstacle clearance during descent to the net level-off altitude
questions.answerText: obstacle clearance during descent to the net level-off altitude
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: How does the lift coefficient for maximum range vary with altitude? (No compressibility effects.)
choices: The lift coefficient decreases with increasing altitude.
The lift coefficient increases with increasing altitude.
Only at low speeds the lift coefficient decreases with increasing altitude.
The lift coefficient is independant of altitude.
questions.answerText: The lift coefficient is independant of altitude.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The absolute ceiling
choices: is the altitude at which the best climb gradient attainable is 5%
is the altitude at which the aeroplane reaches a maximum rate of climb of 100 ft/min.
is the altitude at which the rate of climb theoretically is zero.
can be reached only with minimim steady flight speed
questions.answerText: is the altitude at which the rate of climb theoretically is zero.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The maximum indicated air speed of a piston engined aeroplane, in level flight, is reached:
choices: at the service ceiling.
at the practical ceiling.
at the lowest possible altitude.
at the optimum cruise altitude.
questions.answerText: at the lowest possible altitude.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: In unaccelerated climb
choices: thrust equals drag plus the uphill component of the gross weight in the flight path direction.
thrust equals drag plus the downhill component of the gross weight in the flight path direction.
lift is greater than the gross weight.
lift equals weight plus the vertical component of the drag.
questions.answerText: thrust equals drag plus the downhill component of the gross weight in the flight path direction.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The optimum cruise altitude increases
choices: if the aeroplane mass is decreased.
if the temperature (OAT) is increased.
if the tailwind component is decreased.
if the aeroplane mass is increased.
questions.answerText: if the aeroplane mass is decreased.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Regarding the obstacle limited take-off mass, which of the following statements is correct?
choices: The obstacle limited mass can never be lower than the climb limited take-off mass.
The maximum bank angle which can be used is 10°.
A take-off in the direction of an obstacle is also permitted in tail wind condition.
Wind speed plays no role when calculating this particular mass.
questions.answerText: A take-off in the direction of an obstacle is also permitted in tail wind condition.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane is climbing at a constant IAS and maximum climb thrust, how will the climb angle / the pitch angle change?
choices: Remain constant / decrease.
Remain constant / become larger.
Reduce / decrease.
Reduce / remain constant.
questions.answerText: Reduce / decrease.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Reduced take-off thrust should normally not be used when:
choices: the runway is wet.
the OAT is ISA +10°C
anti skid is not usable.
it is dark.
questions.answerText: anti skid is not usable.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-3591A or Performance Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.5) Consider the take-off performance for the twin jet aeroplane climb limit chart. Why has the wind been omitted from the chart?
choices: There is a built-in safety measure.
The climb limit performances are taken relative to the air.
The effect of the wind must be taken from another chart.
There is no effect of the wind on the climb angle relative to the ground.
questions.answerText: The climb limit performances are taken relative to the air.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: A four jet-engined aeroplane (mass = 150 000 kg) is established on climb with all engines operating. The lift- to-drag ratio is 14. Each engine has a thrust of 75 000 Newtons. The gradient of climb is: (given: g= 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: On a reciprocating engined aeroplane, with increasing altitude at constant gross mass, angle of attack and configuraton the drag
choices: remains unchanged but the TAS increases.
remains unchanged but the the CAS increases.
increases at constant TAS.
decreases and the CAS decreases too because of the lower air density.
questions.answerText: remains unchanged but the TAS increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of factors will increase the climb-limited TOM?
choices: High flap setting, low PA, low OAT.
Low flap setting, high PA, high OAT.
Low flap setting, high PA, low OAT.
Low flap setting, low PA, low OAT.
questions.answerText: Low flap setting, low PA, low OAT.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which statement is correct for a descent without engine thrust at maximum lift to drag ratio speed?
choices: The mass of an aeroplane does not have any effect on the speed for descent.
The higher the gross mass the greater is the speed for descent.
The higher the gross mass the lower is the speed for descent.
The higher the average temperature (OAT) the lower is the speed for descent.
questions.answerText: The higher the gross mass the greater is the speed for descent.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: What will be the influence on the aeroplane performance if aerodrome pressure altitude is increased?
choices: It will increase the take-off distance.
It will decrease the take-off distance.
It will increase the take-off distance available.
It will increase the accelerate stop distance available.
questions.answerText: It will increase the take-off distance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane is in a power off glide at best gliding speed. If the pilot increases pitch attitude the glide distance:
choices: increases.
remains the same.
may increase or decrease depending on the aeroplane.
decreases.
questions.answerText: decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which statement concerning the inclusion of a clearway in take-off calculation is correct?
choices: The field length limited take-off mass will increase.
The usable length of the clearway is not limited.
V1 is increased.
V1 remains constant.
questions.answerText: The field length limited take-off mass will increase.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: What affect has a tailwind on the maximum endurance speed?
choices: No affect
Tailwind only effects holding speed.
The IAS will be increased.
The IAS will be decreased.
questions.answerText: No affect
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the equations below defines specific range (SR)?
choices: SR = Groundspeed/Total Fuel Flow
SR = True Airspeed/Total Fuel Flow
SR = Indicated Airspeed/Total Fuel Flow
SR = Mach Number/Total Fuel Flow
questions.answerText: SR = True Airspeed/Total Fuel Flow
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Take-off performance data, for the ambient conditions, show the following limitations with flap 10° selected: - runway limit: 5 270 kg - obstacle limit: 4 630 kg Estimated take-off mass is 5 000kg. Considering a take-off with flaps at:
choices: 20°, both limitations are increased
5°, the obstacle limit is increased but the runway limit decreases
5°, both limitations are increased
20°, the obstacle limit is increased but the runway limit decreases
questions.answerText: 5°, the obstacle limit is increased but the runway limit decreases
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Is there any difference between the vertical speed versus forward speed curves for two identical aeroplanes having different masses ? (assume zero thrust and wind)
choices: Yes, the difference is that the lighter aeroplane will always glide a greater distance.
Yes, the difference is that for a given angle of attack both the vertical and forward speeds of the heavier aeroplane will be larger.
No difference.
Yes, the difference is that the heavier aeroplane will always glide a greater distance.
questions.answerText: Yes, the difference is that for a given angle of attack both the vertical and forward speeds of the heavier aeroplane will be larger.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements with regard to the optimum cruise altitude (best fuel mileage) is correct?
choices: An aeroplane usually flies above the optimum cruise altitude, as this provides the largest specific range.
An aeroplane sometimes flies above the optimum cruise altitude, because ATC normally does not allow to fly continuously at the optimum cruise altitude.
An aeroplane always flies below the optimum cruise altitude, as otherwise Mach buffet can occur.
An aeroplane always flies on the optimum cruise altitude, because this is most attractive from an economy point of view.
questions.answerText: An aeroplane sometimes flies above the optimum cruise altitude, because ATC normally does not allow to fly continuously at the optimum cruise altitude.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The speed VS is defined as
choices: speed for best specific range.
stalling speed or minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane is controllable.
safety speed for take-off in case of a contaminated runway.
design stress speed.
questions.answerText: stalling speed or minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane is controllable.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6583A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.3) Using the climb performance chart, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the rate of climb and the gradient of climb in the following conditions: Given : O.A.T at Take-o Airport pressure altitude: 3000 ft Aeroplane mass: 3450 lbs Speed: 100 KIAS ff: ISA
choices: 1310 ft/min and 11,3%
1120 ft/min and 9,3%
1030 ft/min and 8,4%
1170 ft/min and 9,9%
questions.answerText: 1120 ft/min and 9,3%
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: How is wind considered in the take-off performance data of the Aeroplane Operations Manuals ?
choices: Unfactored headwind and tailwind components are used.
Not more than 80% headwind and not less than 125% tailwind.
Since take-offs with tailwind are not permitted, only headwinds are considered.
Not more than 50% of a headwind and not less than 150% of the tailwind.
questions.answerText: Not more than 50% of a headwind and not less than 150% of the tailwind.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: If the antiskid system is inoperative, which of the following statements is true?
choices: It has no effect on the accelerate stop distance.
Take-off with antiskid inoperative is not permitted.
The accelerate stop distance increases.
The accelerate stop distance decreases.
questions.answerText: The accelerate stop distance increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A runway is contaminated with 0.5 cm of wet snow. The flight manual of a light twin nevertheless authorises a landing in these conditions. The landing distance will be, in relation to that for a dry runway:
choices: reduced
substantially decreased
increased
unchanged
questions.answerText: increased
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the maximum value for V1 assuming max tyre speed and max brake energy speed are not limiting?
choices: VREF
VR
VMCA
V2
questions.answerText: VR
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The lowest take-off safety speed (V2 min) is:
choices: 1.15 Vs for all turbojet aeroplanes.
1.20 Vs for all turboprop powered aeroplanes.
1.15 Vs for four-engine turboprop aeroplanes and 1.20 Vs for two or three-engine turboprop aeroplanes.
1.20 Vs for all turbojet aeroplanes.
questions.answerText: 1.15 Vs for four-engine turboprop aeroplanes and 1.20 Vs for two or three-engine turboprop aeroplanes.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A 'Balanced Field Length' is said to exist where:
choices: The accelerate stop distance is equal to the take-off distance available.
The clearway does not equal the stopway.
The accelerate stop distance is equal to the all engine take- off distance.
The one engine out take-off distance is equal to the all engine take-off distance.
questions.answerText: The accelerate stop distance is equal to the take-off distance available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-915A) What is the maximum vertical speed of a three engine turbojet aeroplane with one engine inoperative (N-1) and a mass of 75 000 kg? Using the following: g = 10 m/s² 1 kt = 100 ft/min SIN( Angle of climb) = (Thrust- Drag)/ Weight
choices: +3293 ft / min.
+1267 ft / min.
-1267 ft / min.
0 ft / min.
questions.answerText: +1267 ft / min.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Complete the following statement regarding the take-off performance of an aeroplane in performance class A. Following an engine failure at (i) ........... and allowing for a reaction time of (ii) ........... a co rrectly loaded aircraft must be capable of decelerating to a halt within the (iii) .........
choices: (i) V1 (ii) 2 seconds (iii) Accelerate - stop distance available.
(i) V2 (ii) 3 seconds (iii) Take-off distance available.
(i) V1 (ii) 1 second (iii) Accelerate - stop distance available.
(i) V1 (ii) 2 seconds (iii) Take-off distance available.
questions.answerText: (i) V1 (ii) 2 seconds (iii) Accelerate - stop distance available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-3590A or Performance Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.5) With regard to the take-off performance of a twin jet aeroplane, why does the take-off performance climb limit graph show a kink at 30°C, pressure altitude 0?
choices: At lower temperatures one has to take the danger of icing into account.
The engines are pressure limited at lower temperature, at higher temperatures they are temperature limited.
At higher temperatures the flat rated engines determines the climb limit mass.
At higher temperatures the VMBE determines the climb limit mass.
questions.answerText: At higher temperatures the flat rated engines determines the climb limit mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations basically has an effect on the angle of descent in a glide? (Ignore compressibility effects.)
choices: Configuration and mass.
Configuration and angle of attack.
Mass and altitude.
Altitude and configuration.
questions.answerText: Configuration and angle of attack.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The speed V2 is
choices: that speed at which the PIC should decide to continue or not the take-off in the case of an engine failure.
the lowest airspeed required to retract flaps without stall problems.
the lowest safety airspeed at which the aeroplane is under control with aerodynamic surfaces in the case of an engine failure.
the take-off safety speed.
questions.answerText: the take-off safety speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The landing reference speed VREF has, in accordance with international requirements, the following margins above stall speed in landing configuration:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: A higher outside air temperature
choices: does not have any noticeable effect on climb performance.
reduces the angle of climb but increases the rate of climb.
reduces the angle and the rate of climb.
increases the angle of climb but decreases the rate of climb.
questions.answerText: reduces the angle and the rate of climb.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: During the flight preparation a pilot makes a mistake by selecting a V1 greater than that required. Which problem will occur when the engine fails at a speed immediatly above the correct value of V1?
choices: The stop distance required will exceed the stop distance available.
The one engine out take-off distance required may exceed the take-off distance available.
V2 may be too high so that climb performance decreases.
It may lead to over-rotation.
questions.answerText: The stop distance required will exceed the stop distance available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: What is the effect of a head wind component, compared to still air, on the maximum range speed (IAS) and the speed for maximum climb angle respectively?
choices: Maximum range speed decreases and maximum climb angle speed decreases.
Maximum range speed increases and maximum climb angle speed increases.
Maximum range speed increases and maximum climb angle speed stays constant.
Maximum range speed decreases and maximum climb angle speed increases.
questions.answerText: Maximum range speed increases and maximum climb angle speed stays constant.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6573A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.4) With regard to the landing chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the landing distance from a height of 50 ft . Given : O.A.T : ISA +15°C Pressure Altitude: 0 ft Aeroplane Mass: 2940 lbs Headwind component: 10 kt Flaps: Landing position (down) Runway: short and wet grass- firm soil Correction factor (wet grass): 1.38
choices: approximately : 1300 feet
approximately : 2000 feet
approximately : 1450 feet
approximately :1794 feet
questions.answerText: approximately :1794 feet
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The lift coefficient decreases during a glide with constant Mach number, mainly because the :
choices: TAS decreases.
glide angle increases.
IAS increases.
aircraft mass decreases.
questions.answerText: IAS increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The speed V2 of a jet aeroplane must be greater than:
choices: 1.2VMCG.
1.05VLOF.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: When an aircraft takes off with the mass limited by the TODA:
choices: the actual take-off mass equals the field length limited take- off mass.
the distance from brake release to V1 will be equal to the distance from V1 to the 35 feet point.
the "balanced take-off distance" equals 115% of the "all engine take-off distance".
the end of the runway will be cleared by 35 feet following an engine failure at V1.
questions.answerText: the actual take-off mass equals the field length limited take- off mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A runway is contaminated by a 0,5 cm layer of wet snow. The take-off is nevertheless authorized by a ligh t-twin's flight manual. The take-off distance in relation to a dry runway will be:
choices: very significantly decreased
increased
unchanged
decreased
questions.answerText: increased
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The maximum operating altitude for a certain aeroplane with a pressurised cabin
choices: is dependent on aerodynamic ceiling.
is dependent on the OAT.
is only certified for four-engine aeroplanes.
is the highest pressure altitude certified for normal operation.
questions.answerText: is the highest pressure altitude certified for normal operation.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-4744A) Considering a rate of climb diagram (ROC versus TAS) for an aeroplane. Which of the diagrams shows the correct curves for "flaps down" compared to "clean" configuration?
choices: d
a
b
c
questions.answerText: a
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the equations below expresses approximately the unaccelerated percentage climb gradient for small climb angles?
choices: Climb Gradient = ((Thrust - Drag)/Weight) x 100
Climb Gradient = ((Thrust + Drag)/Lift) x 100
Climb Gradient = ((Thrust - Mass)/Lift) x 100
Cimb Gradient = (Lift/Weight) x 100
questions.answerText: Climb Gradient = ((Thrust - Drag)/Weight) x 100
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following di stances will increase if you increase V1?
choices: All Engine Take-off distance
Take-off run
Accelerate Stop Distance
Take-off distance
questions.answerText: Accelerate Stop Distance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: V2 has to be equal to or higher than
choices: 1.1 VMCA.
1.15 VMCG.
1.1 VSO.
questions.answerText: 1.1 VMCA.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: 'Drift down' is the procedure to be applied
choices: to conduct a visual approach if VASI is available.
after engine failure if the aeroplane is above the one engine out maximum altitude.
after cabin depressurization.
to conduct an instrument approach at the alternate.
