questions.answerText: after engine failure if the aeroplane is above the one engine out maximum altitude.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations adversely affects take-off and initial climb performance ?
choices: High temperature and low relative humidity
Low temperature and low relative humidity
High temperature and high relative humidity
Low temperature and high relative humidity
questions.answerText: High temperature and high relative humidity
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which statement regarding V1 is correct ?
choices: When determining V1, reverse thrust may only be used on the remaining symmetric engines
The correction for up-slope on the balanced V1 is negative
VR may not be lower than V1
V1 may not be higher than Vmcg
questions.answerText: VR may not be lower than V1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: During a cruise flight of a jet aeroplane at constant flight level and at the maximum range speed, the IAS / the drag will:
choices: increase / increase.
decrease / increase.
decrease / decrease.
increase / decrease.
questions.answerText: decrease / decrease.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The minimum climb gradient required on the 2nd flight path segment after the take-off of a jet aeroplane is defined by the following parameters: 1 Gear up 2 Gear down 3 Wing flaps retracted 4 Wing flaps in take-off position 5 N engines at the take-off thrust 6 (N-1) engines at the take-off thrust 7 Speed over the path equal to V2 + 10 kt 8 Speed over the path equal to 1.3 VS 9 Speed over the path equal to V2 10 At a height of 35 ft above the runway The correct statements are:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Given that the characteristics of a three engine turbojet aeroplane are as follows: Thrust = 50 000 Newton / Engine g = 10 m/s² Drag = 72 569 N Minimum gross gradient (2nd segment) = 2.7% SIN(Angle of climb) = (Thrust- Drag) / Weight The maximum take-off mass under 2nd segment conditions is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A decrease in atmospheric pressure has, among other things, the following consequences on take-off performance:
choices: a reduced take-off distance and degraded initial climb performance
an increased take-off distance and degraded initial climb performance
a reduced take-off distance and improved initial climb performance
an increased take-off distance and improved initial climb performance
questions.answerText: an increased take-off distance and degraded initial climb performance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following set of factors could lead to a V2 value which is limited by VMCA?
choices: High take-off mass, low flap setting and high field elevation.
Low take-off mass, high flap setting and low field elevation.
Low take-off mass, low flap setting and low field elevation.
High take-off mass, high flap setting and low field elevation.
questions.answerText: Low take-off mass, high flap setting and low field elevation.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The angle of climb with flaps extended, compared to that with flaps retracted, will normally be:
choices: Increase at moderate flap setting, decrease at large flap setting.
Smaller.
Larger.
Not change.
questions.answerText: Smaller.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The critical engine inoperative
choices: does not affect the aeroplane performance since it is independent of the power plant.
decreases the power required because of the lower drag caused by the windmilling engine.
increases the power required and decreases the total drag due to the windmilling engine.
increases the power required because of the greater drag caused by the windmilling engine and the compensation for the yaw effect.
questions.answerText: increases the power required because of the greater drag caused by the windmilling engine and the compensation for the yaw effect.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The lowest point of the drag or thrust required curve of a jet aeroplane, respectively, is the point for
choices: minimum drag.
maximum specific range.
maximum endurance.
minimum specific range.
questions.answerText: minimum drag.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which statement about reduced thrust is correct?
choices: In case of reduced thrust V1 should be decreased.
Reduced thrust can be used when the actual take-off mass is less than the field length limited take-off mass.
Reduced thrust is primarily a noise abatement procedure.
Reduced thrust is used in order to save fuel.
questions.answerText: Reduced thrust can be used when the actual take-off mass is less than the field length limited take-off mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Before take-off the temperature of the wheel brakes should be checked. For what reason?
choices: To ensure that the wheels have warmed up evenly.
To ensure that the thermal blow-out plugs are not melted.
Because overheated brakes will not perform adequately in the event of a rejected take-off.
To ensure that the brake wear is not excessive.
questions.answerText: Because overheated brakes will not perform adequately in the event of a rejected take-off.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The requirements with regard to take-off flight path and the climb segments are only specified for:
choices: the failure of two engines on a multi-engined aeroplane.
the failure of the critical engine on a multi-engines aeroplane.
the failure of any engine on a multi-engined aeroplane.
2 engined aeroplane.
questions.answerText: the failure of the critical engine on a multi-engines aeroplane.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane is climbing with constant IAS. Which operational speed limit is most likely to be reached?
choices: The Stalling speed.
The Minimum control speed air.
The Mach limit for the Mach trim system.
The Maximum operating Mach number.
questions.answerText: The Maximum operating Mach number.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-4743A or Performance Manual MEP1 Figure 3.2) With regard to the graph for the light twin aeroplane, will the accelerate and stop distance be achieved in a take- off where the brakes are released before take-off power is set?
choices: It does not matter which take-off technique is being used.
No, the performance will be worse than in the chart.
Performance will be better than in the chart.
Yes, the chart has been made for this situation.
questions.answerText: No, the performance will be worse than in the chart.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Uphill slope
choices: increases the take-off distance more than the accelerate stop distance.
decreases the accelerate stop distance only.
decreases the take-off distance only.
increases the allowed take-off mass.
questions.answerText: increases the take-off distance more than the accelerate stop distance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: In a given configuration the endurance of a piston engined aeroplane only depends on:
choices: altitude, speed and mass.
speed and mass.
speed, mass and fuel on board.
altitude, speed, mass and fuel on board.
questions.answerText: altitude, speed, mass and fuel on board.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: What is the effect of tail wind on the time to climb to a given altitude?
choices: The time to climb increases.
The time to climb decreases.
The effect on time to climb will depend on the aeroplane type.
The time to climb does not change.
questions.answerText: The time to climb does not change.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The centre of gravity near, but still within, the aft limit
choices: increases the stalling speed.
improves the longitudinal stabiity.
decreases the maximum range.
improves the maximum range.
questions.answerText: improves the maximum range.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: For a jet transport aeroplane, which of the following is the reason for the use of 'maximum range speed' ?
choices: Minimum specific fuel consumption.
Minimum fuel flow.
Longest flight duration.
Minimum drag.
questions.answerText: Minimum specific fuel consumption.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason to operate an aeroplane at 'long range speed'?
choices: The aircraft can be operated close to the buffet onset speed.
In order to prevent loss of speed stability and tuck-under.
It is efficient to fly slightly faster than with maximum range speed.
In order to achieve speed stability.
questions.answerText: It is efficient to fly slightly faster than with maximum range speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The pilot of a single engine aircraft has established the climb performance. The carriage of an additional passenger will cause the climb performance to be:
choices: Degraded
Improved
Unchanged
Unchanged, if a short field take-off is adopted
questions.answerText: Degraded
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The speed for maximum endurance
choices: is always higher than the speed for maximum specific range.
is always lower than the speed for maximum specific range.
is the lower speed to achieve 99% of maximum specific range.
can either be higher or lower than the speed for maximum specific range.
questions.answerText: is always lower than the speed for maximum specific range.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: A headwind component increasing with altitude, as compared to zero wind condition, (assuming IAS is constant)
choices: improves angle and rate of climb.
decreases angle and rate of climb.
has no effect on rate of climb.
does not have any effect on the angle of flight path during climb.
questions.answerText: has no effect on rate of climb.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The intersections of the thrust available and the drag curve are the operating points of the aeroplane
choices: in unaccelerated climb.
in unaccelerated level flight.
in descent with constant IAS.
in accelerated level flight.
questions.answerText: in unaccelerated level flight.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: With respect to the optimum altitude, which of the following statements is correct ?
choices: An aeroplane always flies below the optimum altitude, because Mach buffet might occur.
An aeroplane always flies at the optimum altitude because this is economically seen as the most attractive altitude.
An aeroplane flies most of the time above the optimum altitude because this yields the most economic result.
An aeroplane sometimes flies above or below the optimum altitude because optimum altitude increases continuously during flight.
questions.answerText: An aeroplane sometimes flies above or below the optimum altitude because optimum altitude increases continuously during flight.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: With all other things remaining unchanged and with T the outside static air temperature expressed in degrees K, the hourly fuel consumption of a turbojet powered aeroplane in a cruise flight with a constant Mach Number and zero headwind,is as follows:
choices: proportional to T
proportional to 1/T²
proportional to 1/T
independent from T
questions.answerText: proportional to T
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: To minimize the risk of hydroplaning during landing the pilot should:
choices: make a "positive" landing and apply maximum reverse thrust and brakes as quickly as possible.
use maximum reverse thrust, and should start braking below the hydroplaning speed.
use normal landing-, braking- and reverse technique.
postpone the landing until the risk of hydroplaning no longer exists.
questions.answerText: make a "positive" landing and apply maximum reverse thrust and brakes as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: A firm touchdown followed by timely reverse thrust and firm braking helps shorten the landing roll on wet or contaminated runways.

questions.question: Provided all other parameters stay constant. Which of the following alternatives will decr ease the take-off ground run?
choices: Decreased take-off mass, increased pressure altitude, increased temperature.
Decreased take-off mass, increased density, increased flap setting.
Increased pressure altitude, increased outside air temperature, increased take-off mass.
Increased outside air temperature, decreased pressure altitude, decreased flap setting.
questions.answerText: Decreased take-off mass, increased density, increased flap setting.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: You climb with a climb speed schedule 300/.78. What do you expect in the crossover altitude 29 200 ft (OAT = ISA) ?
choices: During the acceleration to the Mach number .78 the rate of climb is approximately zero.
No noticeable effect since the true airspeed at 300 kt IAS and .78 Mach are the same (at ISA temperature TAS=460 kt)
The rate of climb increases since the constant IAS-climb is replaced by the constant Mach-climb.
The rate of climb decreases since climb performance at a constant Mach number is grossly reduced as compared to constant IAS.
questions.answerText: The rate of climb increases since the constant IAS-climb is replaced by the constant Mach-climb.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6587A or Flight planning Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.4) Using the Range Profile Diagramm, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the range, with 45 minutes reserve, in the following conditions: Given : O.A.T.: ISA +16°C Pressure altitude: 4000 ft Power: Full throttle / 25,0 in/Hg./ 2100 RPM
choices: 851 NM
911 NM
865 NM
739 NM
questions.answerText: 865 NM
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: V1 has to be
choices: equal to or higher than VMCG.
equal to or higher than VMCA.
higher than than VR.
equal to or higher than V2.
questions.answerText: equal to or higher than VMCG.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: An aircraft has two certified landing flaps positions, 25° and 35°. If a pilot chooses 25° instead of 35°, the aircraft will have:
choices: a reduced landing distance and better go-around performance
an increased landing distance and degraded go-around performance
a reduced landing distance and degraded go-around performance
an increased landing distance and better go-around performance
questions.answerText: an increased landing distance and better go-around performance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: An aircraft has two certified landing flaps positions, 25° and 35°. If a pilot chooses 35° instead of 25°, the aircraft will have:
choices: an increased landing distance and better go-around performance
a reduced landing distance and degraded go-around performance
a reduced landing distance and better go-around performance
an increased landing distance and degraded go-around performance
questions.answerText: a reduced landing distance and degraded go-around performance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The take-off safety speed V2min for turbo-propeller powered aeroplanes with more than three engines may not be less than:
choices: 1.3 Vs
1.2 Vs
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is true with regard to VMCA (air minimum control speed)?
choices: The aeroplane is uncontrollable below VMCA
The aeroplane will not gather the minimum required climb gradient
VMCA only applies to four-engine aeroplanes
Straight flight can not be maintained below VMCA, when the critical engine has failed.
questions.answerText: Straight flight can not be maintained below VMCA, when the critical engine has failed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Minimum control speed on ground, VMCG, is based on directional control being maintained by:
choices: nosewheel steering only.
primary aerodynamic control only.
primary aerodynamic control and nosewheel.
primary aerodynamic control, nosewheel steering and differential braking.
questions.answerText: primary aerodynamic control only.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: What is the advantage of a balanced field length condition ?
choices: For a balanced field length the required take-off runway length always equals the available runway length.
A balanced field length provides the greatest margin between "net" and "gross" take-off flight paths.
A balanced field length gives the minimum required field length in the event of an engine failure.
A balanced take-off provides the lowest elevator input force requirement for rotation.
questions.answerText: A balanced field length gives the minimum required field length in the event of an engine failure.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane is performing a maximum range flight. The speed corresponds to:
choices: the minimum drag.
the minimum required power.
the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the power required (Pr) versus TAS curve.
the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the Drag versus TAS curve.
questions.answerText: the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the Drag versus TAS curve.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements, concerning the obstacle limited take-off mass for performance class A aeroplane, is correct?
choices: It should not be corrected for 30° bank turns in the take-off path.
It should be calculated in such a way that there is a margin of 50 ft with respect to the "net take off flight path".
It cannot be lower than the corresponding climb limited take- off mass.
It should be determined on the basis of a 35 ft obstacle clearance with the respect to the "net take-off flight path".
questions.answerText: It should be determined on the basis of a 35 ft obstacle clearance with the respect to the "net take-off flight path".
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The airspeed for jet aeroplanes at which power required is a minimum
choices: is always higher than the minimum drag speed.
is lower than the minimum drag speed in the climb and higher than the minimum drag speed in the descent.
is the same as the minimum drag speed.
is always lower than the minimum drag speed.
questions.answerText: is always lower than the minimum drag speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Take-off run is defined as the
choices: Distance from brake release to V2.

horizontal distance along the take-off path from the start of the take-off to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 ft above the take-off surface.
distance to V1 and stop, assuming an engine failure at V1.
distance to 35 feet with an engine failure at V1 or 115% all engine distance to 35 feet.
questions.answerText: horizontal distance along the take-off path from the start of the take-off to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 ft above the take-off surface.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Long range cruise is a flight procedure which gives:
choices: an IAS which is 1% higher than the IAS for maximum specific range.
a specific range which is 99% of maximum specific range and a lower cruise speed.
a specific range which is about 99% of maximum specific range and higher cruise speed.
a 1% higher TAS for maximum specific range.
questions.answerText: a specific range which is about 99% of maximum specific range and higher cruise speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The thrust of a jet engine at constant RPM
choices: does not change with changing altitude.
is independent of the airspeed.
is inversely proportional to the airspeed.
increases in proportion to the airspeed.
questions.answerText: increases in proportion to the airspeed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: During the flight preparation the climb limited take-off mass (TOM) is found to be much greater than the field length limited TOM using 5° flap. In what way can the performance limited TOM be increased? There are no limiting obstacles.
choices: By selecting a higher flap setting.
By selecting a higher V2.
By selecting a lower V2.
By selecting a lower flap setting.
questions.answerText: By selecting a higher flap setting.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: If the value of the balanced V1 is found to be lower than VMCG, which of the following is correct ?
choices: The ASDR will become greater than the one engine out take- off distance.
The take-off is not permitted.
The one engine out take-off distance will become greater than the ASDR.
The VMCG will be lowered to V1.
questions.answerText: The take-off is not permitted.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
choices: VR is the speed at which rotation should be initiated.
VR is the lowest climb speed after engine failure.
In case of engine failure below VR the take-off should be aborted.
VR is the lowest speed for directional control in case of engine failure.
questions.answerText: VR is the speed at which rotation should be initiated.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: A twin engined aeroplane in cruise flight with one engine inoperative has to fly over high ground. In order to maintain the highest possible altitude the pilot should choose:
choices: the speed corresponding to the minimum value of (lift / drag)^3/2.
the speed at the maximum lift.
the speed corresponding to the maximum value of the lift / drag ratio.
the long range speed.
questions.answerText: the speed corresponding to the maximum value of the lift / drag ratio.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6581A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.3) Using the climb performance chart, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the ground distance to reach a height of 2000 ft above the reference zero inthe following conditions: Given : O.A.T. at take-o ff: 25°C Airport pressure altitude: 1000 ft Aeroplane mass: 3600 lbs Speed: 100 KIAS Wind component: 15 kts Headwind
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: At speeds below minimum drag
choices: the aeroplane can be controlled only in level flight.
a lower speed requires a higher thrust.
a higher speed requires a higher thrust.
the aeroplane can not be controlled manually.
questions.answerText: a lower speed requires a higher thrust.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following are to be taken into account for the runway in use for take-off ?
choices: Airport elevation, runway slope, standard temperature, pressure altitude and wind components.
Airport elevation, runway slope, outside air temperature, standard pressure and wind components.
Airport elevation, runway slope, outside air temperature, pressure altitude and wind components.
Airport elevation, runway slope, standard temperature, standard pressure and wind components.
questions.answerText: Airport elevation, runway slope, outside air temperature, pressure altitude and wind components.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: To achieve the maximum range over ground with headwind the airspeed should be
choices: lower compared to the speed for maximum range cruise with no wind.
reduced to the gust penetration speed.
higher compared to the speed for maximum range cruise with no wind.
equal to the speed for maximum range cruise with no wind.
questions.answerText: higher compared to the speed for maximum range cruise with no wind.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Required runway length at destination airport for turboprop aeroplanes
choices: is the same as at an alternate airport.
is less then at an alternate airport.
is more than at an alternate airport.
is 60% longer than at an alternate airport.
questions.answerText: is the same as at an alternate airport.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: May anti-skid be considered to determine the take-off and landing data ?
choices: Only for take-off.
Only for landing.
Yes.
No.
questions.answerText: Yes.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6578A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.2) With regard to the take off performance chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the take off distance to a height of 50 ft. Given : O.A.T : 38°C Pressure Altitude: 4000 ft Aeroplane Mass: 3400 lbs Tailwind component: 5 kt Flaps: Approach setting Runway: Dry Grass Correction factor: 1.2
choices: approximately : 3680 ft
approximately : 4200 ft
approximately : 5040 ft
approximately : 3960 ft
questions.answerText: approximately : 3960 ft
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The take-off decision speed V1 is:
choices: a chosen limit. If an engine failure is recognized before reaching V1 the take-off must be aborted.
not less than V2min, the minimum take-off safety speed.
a chosen limit. If an engine failure is recognized after reaching V1 the take-off must be aborted.
sometimes greater than the rotation speed VR.
questions.answerText: a chosen limit. If an engine failure is recognized before reaching V1 the take-off must be aborted.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The speed VLO is defined as
choices: lift off speed.
landing gear operating speed.
design low operating speed.
long distance operating speed.
questions.answerText: landing gear operating speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane operating under the 180 minutes ETOPS rule may be up to :
choices: 180 minutes flying time to a suitable airport in still air with one engine inoperative.
180 minutes flying time to a suitable airport under the prevailing weather condition with one engine inoperative.
180 minutes flying time from suitable airport in still air at a normal cruising speed
90 minutes flying time from the first enroute airport and another 90 minutes from the second enroute airport in still air with one engine inoperative.
questions.answerText: 180 minutes flying time to a suitable airport in still air with one engine inoperative.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: If the airworthiness documents do not specify a correction for landing on a wet runway; the landing distance must be increased by:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The 'climb gradient' is defined as the ratio of
choices: true airspeed to rate of climb.
rate of climb to true airspeed.
the increase of altitude to horizontal air distance expressed as a percentage.
the increase of altitude to distance over ground expressed as a percentage.
questions.answerText: the increase of altitude to horizontal air distance expressed as a percentage.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The take-off distance required increases
choices: due to slush on the runway.
due to downhill slope because of the smaller angle of attack.
due to head wind because of the drag augmentation.
due to lower gross mass at take-off.
questions.answerText: due to slush on the runway.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Following a take-off, limited by the 50 ft screen height, a light twin climbs on a gradient of 5%. It will clear a 160 m obstacle in relation to the runway (horizontally), situated at 5 000 m from the 50 ft point with an obstacle clearance margin of:
choices: it will not clear the obstacle
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-4733A or Performance Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.28) What is the minimum field length required for the worst wind situation, landing a twin jet aeroplane with the anti- skid inoperative? Elevation: 2000 ft QNH: 1013 hPa Landing mass: 50 000 kg Flaps: as required for minimum landing distance Runway condition: dry Wind: Maximum allowable tailwind: 15 kt Maximum allowable headwind: 50 kt
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The take-off performance requirements for transport category aeroplanes are based upon:
choices: failure of critical engine.
failure of critical engine or all engines operating which ever gives the largest take off distance.
all engines operating.
only one engine operating.
questions.answerText: failure of critical engine or all engines operating which ever gives the largest take off distance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-2929A) Consider the graphic representation of the power required versus true air speed (TAS), for a piston engined aeroplane with a given mass. When drawing the tangent from the origin, the point of contact (A) determines the speed of:
choices: maximum thrust.
critical angle of attack.
maximum specific range.
maximum endurance.
questions.answerText: maximum specific range.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The aerodynamic ceiling
choices: is the altitude at which the aeroplane reaches 50 ft/min.
is the altitude at which the speeds for low speed buffet and for high speed buffet are the same.
depends upon thrust setting and increase with increasing thrust.
is the altitude at which the best rate of climb theoretically is zero.
questions.answerText: is the altitude at which the speeds for low speed buffet and for high speed buffet are the same.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: In which of the flight conditions listed below is the thrust required (Tr) equal to the drag (D)?
choices: In a descent with constant TAS
In level flight with constant IAS
In accelerated level flight
In a climb with constant IAS
questions.answerText: In level flight with constant IAS
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct? If the aircraft mass, in a horizontal unaccelerated flight, decreases
choices: the minimum drag decreases and the IAS for minimum drag decreases.
the minimum drag increases and the IAS for minimum drag decreases.
the minimum drag increases and the IAS for minimum drag increases.
the minimum drag decreases and the IAS for minimum drag increases.
questions.answerText: the minimum drag decreases and the IAS for minimum drag decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the minimum for V1?
choices: VMU
VR
VMCG
VLOF
questions.answerText: VMCG
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The landing field length required for turbojet aeroplanes at the destination (wet condition) is the demonstrated landing distance plus
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Other factors remaining constant and not limiting, how does increasing pressure altitude affect allowable take- off mass?
choices: Allowable take-off mass remains uninfluenced up to 5000 ft PA.
Allowable take-off mass decreases.
Allowable take-off mass increases.
There is no effect on allowable take-off mass.
questions.answerText: Allowable take-off mass decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: If other factors are unchanged, the fuel mileage (nautical miles per kg) is
choices: independent from the centre of gravity position.
lower with an aft centre of gravity position.
higher with a forward centre of gravity position.
lower with a forward centre of gravity position.
questions.answerText: lower with a forward centre of gravity position.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: For a turbojet aeroplane, what is the maximum landing distance for wet runways when the landing distance available at an aerodrome is 3000 m?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
choices: The climb limited take-off mass increases when a larger take-off flap setting is used.
The climb limited take-off mass depends on pressure altitude and outer air temperature
The performance limited take-off mass is the highest of: field length limited take-off mass climb limited take-off mass obstacle limited take-off mass.
The climb limited take-off mass will increase if the headwind component increases.
questions.answerText: The climb limited take-off mass depends on pressure altitude and outer air temperature
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Changing the take-off flap setting from flap 15° to flap 5° will normally result in :
choices: a longer take-off distance and a better climb.
a shorter take-off distance and an equal climb.
a better climb and an equal take-off distance.
a shorter take-off distance and a better climb.
questions.answerText: a longer take-off distance and a better climb.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-11661A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.1) An extract of the flight manual of a single engine propeller aircraft is reproduced in annex. Airport characteristics: hard, dry and zero slope runway Actual conditions are: pressure altitude: 1 500 ft outside tempereature: +18°C wind component: 4 knots tailwind For a take-off mass of 1 270 kg , the take-off distance will be:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The take-off mass of an aeroplane is restricted by the climb limit. What would be the effect on this limit of an increase in the headwind component?
choices: The climb limited take-off mass would decrease.
None.
The effect would vary depending upon the height of any obstacle within the net take-off flight path.
The climb limited take-off mass would increase.
questions.answerText: None.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6569A or Performance Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.4) With regard to the landing chart for the single engine aeroplane determine the landing distance from a height of 50 ft . Given : O.A.T : 27 °C Pressure Altitude: 3000 ft Aeroplane Mass: 2900 lbs Tailwind component: 5 kt Flaps: Landing position (down) Runway: Tarred and Dry
choices: approximately : 1120 feet
approximately : 1700 feet
approximately : 1370 feet
approximately : 1850 feet
questions.answerText: approximately : 1850 feet
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The speed for maximum lift/drag ratio will result in :
choices: The maximum endurance for a propeller driven aeroplane.
The maximum angle of climb for a propeller driven aeroplane.
The maximum range for a propeller driven aeroplane.
The maximum range for a jet aeroplane.
questions.answerText: The maximum range for a propeller driven aeroplane.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: In the event that the take-off mass is obstacle limited and the take-off flight path includes a turn, the bank angle should not exceed
choices: 10 degrees up to a height of 400 ft.
20 degrees up to a height of 400 ft.
25 degrees up to a height of 400 ft.
15 degrees up to height of 400 ft.
questions.answerText: 15 degrees up to height of 400 ft.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The one engine out take-off run is the distance between the brake release point and:
choices: the point half way between V1 and V2.
the middle of the segment between VLOF point and 35 ft point.
the lift-off point.
the point where V2 is reached.
questions.answerText: the middle of the segment between VLOF point and 35 ft point.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which take-off speed is affected by the presence or absence of stopway and/or clearway ?
choices: V2
VMCG
VMCA
V1
questions.answerText: V1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The take-off mass could be limited by
choices: the take-off distance available (TODA), the maximum brake energy and the climb gradient with one engine inoperative.
the maximum brake energy only.
the climb gradient with one engine inoperative only.
the take-off distance available (TODA) only.
questions.answerText: the take-off distance available (TODA), the maximum brake energy and the climb gradient with one engine inoperative.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: If a flight is performed with a higher "Cost Index" at a given mass which of the following will occur?
choices: A better long range.
A higher cruise mach number.
A lower cruise mach number.
A better maximum range.
questions.answerText: A higher cruise mach number.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: What is the influence of the mass on maximum rate of climb (ROC) speed if all other parameters remain constant ?
choices: The ROC is affected by the mass, but not the ROC speed.
The ROC and the ROC speed are independant of the mass.
The ROC speed increases with increasing mass.
The ROC speed decreases with increasing mass.
questions.answerText: The ROC speed increases with increasing mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: During a descent at constant Mach Number, the margin to low speed buffet will:
choices: decrease, because the lift coefficient decreases.
increase, because the lift coefficient decreases.
remain constant, because the Mach number remains constant.
increase, because the lift coefficient increases.
questions.answerText: increase, because the lift coefficient decreases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The net flight path climb gradient after take-off compared to the gross climb gradient is:
choices: larger.
equal.
depends on type of aircraft.
smaller.
questions.answerText: smaller.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: An operator shall ensure that the net take-off flight path clears all obstacles. The half-width of the obstacle- corridor at the distance D from the end of the TODA is at least:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: How does runway slope affect allowable take-off mass, assuming other factors remain constant and not limiting?
choices: An uphill slope increases take-off mass.
Allowable take-off mass is not affected by runway slope.
A downhill slope decreases allowable take-off mass.
A downhill slope increases allowable take-off mass.
questions.answerText: A downhill slope increases allowable take-off mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The maximum rate of climb that can be maintained at the absolute ceiling is:
choices: 0 ft/min
125 ft/min
500 ft/min
100 ft/min
questions.answerText: 0 ft/min
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: At which minimum height will the second climb segment end?
choices: 1500 ft above field elevation.
400 ft above field elevation.
35 ft above ground.
When gear retraction is completed.
questions.answerText: 400 ft above field elevation.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: In case of an engine failure recognized below V1
choices: the take-off must be rejected.
the take-off may be continued if a clearway is available.
the take-off should only be rejected if a stopway is available.
the take-off is to be continued unless V1 is less than the balanced V1.
questions.answerText: the take-off must be rejected.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: On a segment of the take-off flight path an obstacle requires a minimum gradient of climb of 2.6% in order to provide an adequate margin of safe clearance. At a mass of 110000 kg the gradient of climb is 2.8%. For the same power and assuming that the sine of the angle of climb varies inversely with mass, at what maximum mass will the aeroplane be able to achieve the minimum gradient?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The take-off safety speed V2 for two-engined or three- engined turbo propeller powered aeroplanes may not be less than:
choices: 1.3 Vs
1.2 Vs
questions.answerText: 1.2 Vs
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The pilot of a jet aeroplane wants to use a minimum amount of fuel between two airfields. Which flight procedure should the pilot fly?
choices: Maximum endurance.
Holding.
Long range.
Maximum range.
questions.answerText: Maximum range.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: When V1 has to be reduced because of a wet runway the one engine out obstacle clearance / climb performance:
choices: increases / increases.
remains constant / remains constant.
decreases / decreases.
decreases / remains constant.
questions.answerText: decreases / remains constant.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Density altitude is the
choices: altitude read directly from the altimeter
height above the surface
pressure altitude corrected for 'non standard' temperature
altitude reference to the standard datum plane
questions.answerText: pressure altitude corrected for 'non standard' temperature
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An increase in atmospheric pressure has, among other things, the following consequences on landing performance:
choices: a reduced landing distance and degraded go around performance
a reduced landing distance and improved go-around performance
an increased landing distance and degraded go-around performance
an increased landing distance and improved go-around performance
questions.answerText: a reduced landing distance and improved go-around performance
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Approaching in turbulent wind conditions requires a change in the landing reference speed (VREF):
choices: Increasing VREF
Lowering VREF
Keeping same VREF because wind has no influence on IAS.
Increasing VREF and making a steeper glide path to avoid the use of spoilers.
questions.answerText: Increasing VREF
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: What margin above the stall speed is provided by the landing reference speed VREF?
choices: 1,10 VSO
VMCA x 1,2
1,30 VSO
1,05 VSO
questions.answerText: 1,30 VSO
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The speed V1 is defined as
choices: take-off climb speed.
speed for best angle of climb.
engine failure speed.
take-off decision speed.
questions.answerText: take-off decision speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: A multi engine aeroplane is flying at the minimum control speed (VMCA). Which parameter(s) must be maintainable after engine failure?
choices: Heading, altitude and a positive rate of climb of 100 ft/min
Altitude
Straight flight
Straight flight and altitude
questions.answerText: Straight flight
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Long range cruise is selected as
choices: the higher speed to achieve 99% of maximum specific range in zero wind.
the speed for best economy.
the climbing cruise with one or two engines inoperative.
specific range with tailwind.
questions.answerText: the higher speed to achieve 99% of maximum specific range in zero wind.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: An airport has a 3000 metres long runway, and a 2000 metres clearway at each end of that runway. For the calculation of the maximum allowed take-off mass, the take-off distance available cannot be greater than:
choices: 6000 metres.
4000 metres.
5000 metres.
4500 metres.
questions.answerText: 4500 metres.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The length of a clearway may be included in:
choices: the accelerate-stop distance available.
the take-off run available.
the distance to reach V1.
the take-off distance available.
questions.answerText: the take-off distance available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: What happens when an aeroplane climbs at a constant Mach number?
choices: IAS stays constant so there will be no problems.
The "1.3G" altitude is exceeded, so Mach buffet will start immediately.
The lift coefficient increases.
The TAS continues to increase, which may lead to structural problems.
questions.answerText: The lift coefficient increases.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: A higher altitude at constant mass and Mach number requires
choices: a lower coefficient of drag.
a lower angle of attack.
a higher angle of attack.
a lower coefficient of lift.
questions.answerText: a higher angle of attack.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The decision speed at take-off (V1) is the calibrated airspeed:
choices: at which the take-off must be rejected.
below which the take-off must be continued.
at which the failure of the critical engine is expected to occur.
below which take-off must be rejected if an engine failure is recognized, above which take-off must be continued.
questions.answerText: below which take-off must be rejected if an engine failure is recognized, above which take-off must be continued.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 032-6584A or Flight Planning Manual SEP 1 Figure 2.2 Table 2.2.3) Using the Power Setting Table, for the single engine aeroplane, determine the manifold pressure and fuel flow (lbs/hr) with full throttle and cruise lean mixture in the following conditions: Given: OAT: 13°C Pressure altitude: 8000 ft RPM: 2300
choices: 22,4 in.Hg and 73,8 lbs/hr
22,4 in.Hg and 69,3 lbs/hr
23,0 in.Hg and 69,0 lbs/hr
22,4 in.Hg and 71,1 lbs/hr
questions.answerText: 22,4 in.Hg and 69,3 lbs/hr
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Why are 'step climbs' used on long distance flights ?
choices: Step climbs do not have any special purpose for jet aeroplanes; they are used for piston engine aeroplanes only.
To respect ATC flight level constraints.
To fly as close as possible to the optimum altitude as aeroplane mass reduces.
Step climbs are only justified if at the higher altitude less headwind or more tailwind can be expected.
questions.answerText: To fly as close as possible to the optimum altitude as aeroplane mass reduces.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: In the event of engine failure below V1, the first action to be taken by the pilot in order to decelerate the aeroplane is to:
choices: apply wheel brakes.
deploy airbrakes or spoilers.
reduce the engine thrust.
reverse engine thrust.
questions.answerText: reduce the engine thrust.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

Maximum Landing Distance at the destination aerodrome and at any alternate aerodrome is 0,7 x LDA (Landing Distance Available).
Maximum Landing Distance at destination is 0,95 x LDA (Landing Distance Available).
questions.answerText: Maximum Landing Distance at the destination aerodrome and at any alternate aerodrome is 0,7 x LDA (Landing Distance Available).
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Under which condition should you fly considerably lower (4 000 ft or more) than the optimum altitude ?
choices: If at the lower altitude either more headwind or less tailwind can be expected.
If at the lower altitude either considerably less headwind or considerably more tailwind can be expected.
If the maximum altitude is below the optimum altitude.
If the temperature is lower at the low altitude (high altitude inversion).
questions.answerText: If at the lower altitude either considerably less headwind or considerably more tailwind can be expected.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is applicable to the acceleration height at the beginning of the 3rd climb segment ?
choices: The minimum legally allowed acceleration height is at 1500 ft.
There is no requirement for minimum climb performance when flying at the acceleration height.
The minimum one engine out acceleration height must be maintained in case of all engines operating.
The maximum acceleration height depends on the maximum time take-off thrust may be applied.
questions.answerText: The maximum acceleration height depends on the maximum time take-off thrust may be applied.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which statement regarding V1 is correct?
choices: V1 is not allowed to be greater than VMCG.
When determining the V1, reverse thrust is only allowed to be taken into account on the remaining symmetric engines.
The V1 correction for up-slope is negative.
V1 is not allowed to be greater than VR.
questions.answerText: V1 is not allowed to be greater than VR.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The 'maximum tyre speed' limits:
choices: VR, or VMU if this is lower than VR.
V1 in kt ground speed.
VLOF in terms of ground speed.
V1 in kt TAS.
questions.answerText: VLOF in terms of ground speed.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The result of a higher flap setting up to the optimum at take-off is
choices: a higher V1.
a longer take-off run.
a shorter ground roll.
an increased acceleration.
questions.answerText: a shorter ground roll.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following provides maximum obstacle clearance during climb?
choices: The speed for maximum rate of climb.
The speed, at which the flaps may be selected one position further UP.
The speed for maximum climb angle Vx.
questions.answerText: The speed for maximum climb angle Vx.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: In relation to the net take-off flight path, the required 35 ft vertical distance to clear all obstacles is
choices: based on pressure altitudes.
the height by which acceleration and flap retraction should be completed.
the height at which power is reduced to maximum climb thrust.
the minimum vertical distance between the lowest part of the aeroplane and all obstacles within the obstacle corridor.
questions.answerText: the minimum vertical distance between the lowest part of the aeroplane and all obstacles within the obstacle corridor.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The stopway is an area which allows an increase only in :
choices: the accelerate-stop distance available.
the take-off run available.
the take-off distance available.
the landing distance available.
questions.answerText: the accelerate-stop distance available.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The coefficient of lift can be increased either by flap extension or by
choices: increasing the CAS.
increasing the angle of attack.
increasing the TAS.
decreasing the 'nose-up' elevator trim setting.
questions.answerText: increasing the angle of attack.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: If the field length limited take off mass has been calculated using a Balanced Field Length technique, the use of any additional clearway in take off performance calculations may allow
choices: a greater field length limited take off mass but with a higher V1
the obstacle clearance limit to be increased with no effect on V1
the obstacle clearance limit to be increased with an higher V1
a greater field length limited take off mass but with a lower V1
questions.answerText: a greater field length limited take off mass but with a lower V1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: An engine failure at high cruising altitude will always result in a drift down, because it is not permitted to fly the same altitude as with all engines operating.
When determining the obstacle clearance during drift down, fuel dumping may be taken into account.
The drift down regulations require a minimum descent angle after an engine failure at cruising altitude.
The drift down procedure requires a minimum obstacle clearance of 35 ft.
questions.answerText: When determining the obstacle clearance during drift down, fuel dumping may be taken into account.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The take-off run is
choices: the horizontal distance along the take-off path from the start of the take-off to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 ft above the take-off surface.

1.5 times the distance from the point of brake release to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane attains a height of 35 ft above the runway with all engines operative.
1.15 times the distance from the point of brake release to the point at which VLOF is reached assuming a failure of the critical engine at V1.

the distance of the point of brake release to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane attains a height of 50 ft above the runway assuming a failure of the critical engine at V1.
questions.answerText: the horizontal distance along the take-off path from the start of the take-off to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 ft above the take-off surface.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The use of reduced take-off thrust is permitted, only if:
choices: The actual take-off mass (TOM) is greater than the climb limited TOM.
The actual take-off mass (TOM) is lower than the field length limited TOM.
The take-off distance available is lower than the take-off distance required one engine out at V1.
The actual take-off mass (TOM) including a margin is greater than the performance limited TOM.
questions.answerText: The actual take-off mass (TOM) is lower than the field length limited TOM.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: With one or two engines inoperative the best specific range at high altitudes is
choices: first improved and later reduced.
reduced.
improved.
not affected.
questions.answerText: reduced.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane equipped with old engines has a specific fuel consumption of 0.06 kg per Newton of thrust and per hour and, in a given flying condition, a fuel mileage of 14 kg per Nautical Mile. In the same flying conditions, the same aeroplane equipped with modern engines with a specific fuel consumption of 0.035 kg per Newton of thrust and per hour, has a fuel mileage of:
choices: 10.7 kg/NM.
8.17 kg/NM.
14 kg/NM.
11.7 kg/NM.
questions.answerText: 8.17 kg/NM.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.
